Hi Daniela, it is Sarah, your English coach. You are going to write a lot of emails to the US team, so here are my four email tips. First, the subject line. Make it short and clear, so people know what the email is about before they open it. For example: Status call, agenda for Monday. Second, the first sentence. Say why you are writing. I am writing to ask about the store data, or I am writing regarding the November call. Third, the request. Americans are friendly, but they are busy. So be polite and direct at the same time. Could you send me the report by Friday? Or, I would appreciate it if you could confirm the time. One request per paragraph is best. And fourth, the sign-off. With your manager or a new contact, use Best regards. With a colleague you know well, Thanks or Best is fine. Before you click send, read your email one more time, and check the attachment. Everybody forgets it sometimes. Good luck with your emails, Daniela.

Hi Daniela, it is Greg. Quick message about the status call in November. Before you start, I need you to send three emails this week. First, a request to Jennifer on the US team. Could you ask her for the store sales data for October? She has it in a spreadsheet, and she can send it as an attachment. Second, a follow-up to Mark. He has not replied to my email about the call time, so please send him a short follow-up regarding the Monday meeting. Be friendly, he is very busy. And third, a thank-you to the London team. They helped us a lot with the budget review, so a short thank-you email will be great. Please copy me on all three. Thanks, Daniela. I know they will be great.

First, Daniela wrote a clear subject line: Store data for October. Then she opened with a friendly greeting: Hi Jennifer, I hope you are well. After that, she said why she was writing: I am writing to ask about the store sales data. Next, she made a polite request: Could you send me the spreadsheet as an attachment by Friday? Finally, she closed with a thank-you and a sign-off: Thanks in advance. Best regards, Daniela.
